title: Enum with Data
story: Your weather app needs to report more than just "Rainy" — how much rain? And "Snowy" needs the snow depth. You need variants that carry data with them!
why: Enum variants with data let each option carry its own relevant information — millimeters of rain, centimeters of snow, or nothing at all for Sunny.
analogy: Enums with data are like labeled boxes — the label says what's inside (Rainy), and when you open the box (match), you find the payload (millimeters of rain).
try_it: Add a `Windy(kph: Float64)` variant to the Weather enum. Update `report` to handle it. Test with Windy(45.0) and Windy(10.0).
tips: Variants with data use `()` after the name with typed fields: `Rainy(mm: Float64)`
In match, the pattern variable grabs the payload: `Rainy(mm) => ...` — then you use `mm` like any variable
Use `_` as a catch-all: `_ => false` means "for every variant I didn't explicitly list"
common_mistakes: Using parentheses on simple variants: `Weather.Sunny()` is wrong — only data variants need `()`
Forgetting to name the payload field in match: `Rainy => ...` won't let you access the mm value
Treating the payload like a struct field: `weather.mm` doesn't work — you must use match to extract it
